artifacts.layman_summary: Trains a small image classifier two ways and checks whether the sharpness-aware method makes its confidence scores more trustworthy without losing accuracy.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_1
artifacts.summary: Artifact: a controlled comparison of plain SGD (momentum 0.9) against sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) on a two-block CNN trained on Fashion-MNIST. Both optimizers share architecture, data split (50k/10k/10k from the 60k training images, official 10k test), batch size, schedule, weight decay and per-seed initialization and batch order. Learning rates (and SAM's rho) were chosen on validation NLL only, using seed 100. Final results use 5 paired seeds (0-4) at 40 epochs, plus compressed 5- and 15-epoch schedules to test whether the calibration gap grows with training length. A temperature-scaled SGD control is fitted on validation logits. Reported metrics: accuracy, ECE (15 equal-width bins), ACE, NLL, Brier, AURC, with paired t-intervals (df=4), Holm correction and reliability diagrams. Key results at epoch 40 (SAM minus SGD): accuracy +0.0015 with CI [-0.0007, +0.0036] (no detectable difference); ECE -0.0378 [-0.0414, -0.0341]; NLL -0.0980 [-0.1092, -0.0867]; Brier -0.0136; AURC -0.0015. Against temperature-scaled SGD, SAM's NLL is still lower (-0.0209 [-0.0266, -0.0151], Holm p=0.0027), but its ECE advantage is not significant after Holm (p=0.079). Caveats: SAM is under-fit at epoch 40 (training loss 0.107 against 0.008 for SGD), so part of its calibration advantage may come from a less-fit model; both selected learning rates (0.01) sit at the lower edge of the grid; one tuning configuration collapsed to chance (SAM lr 0.03, rho 0.2) and was not selected; the 60-epoch extension was not run. Scope is one dataset and one small architecture, with five seeds, so power is low. Independent re-derivation: the headline paired differences and CIs were recomputed directly from the saved test logits with separate code (explicit log-softmax and bin loops, scipy ttest_rel), and matched to the reported values; placebo checks (identical models, permuted labels) did not reject. Not re-derived: the ECE bin loop and ACE/Brier/AURC for every run were not independently recomputed, and the training itself was not repeated.
artifacts.title: Does SAM Improve Calibration on Fashion-MNIST?

artifacts.layman_summary: We train the same small image classifier two ways on clothing photos and check whether the sharper-minimum training method makes its confidence more trustworthy, and whether that benefit comes from avoiding overfitting.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_2
artifacts.summary: Mechanism sub-experiment on whether Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) calibration gains track overfitting. A small CNN (two conv blocks with batch norm and 2x2 max pooling, then two linear layers) is trained on Fashion-MNIST, validation split 10k, official test 10k, with plain SGD and with SAM (rho 0.1) for seeds 0, 1 and 2, under one pre-specified configuration: lr 0.03, momentum 0.9, weight decay 5e-4, batch 128, 60 epochs, cosine schedule. Both optimisers share the initialisation and data order per seed. Per-epoch training loss and validation ECE, NLL, Brier and adaptive calibration error, the top Hessian eigenvalue (power iteration, 20 iterations, fixed 2000-image batch) and the SAM rho-ball loss increase are in results/per_epoch.json. Test logits at epochs 5 and 60 feed test metrics and a temperature-scaling control fitted on validation only. Headline results at epoch 60 (descriptive, n=3): SAM test ECE 0.028 vs SGD 0.045 (mean difference -0.017, all seeds negative), SAM test NLL lower by 0.076, test accuracy difference +0.001 with mixed signs. Under temperature scaling the gap shrinks to 0.007 vs 0.009, so much of the advantage is a global confidence shift. SGD reaches training loss 0.0045 while SAM stays near 0.03. At matched training loss, SAM has a top Hessian eigenvalue about 12 to 16 lower and validation ECE about 0.010 to 0.014 lower. Epoch-5 calibration differences have no consistent sign. No p-values are reported; with 3 seed pairs no test can reach conventional significance. Files: method.py (training, unit checks, analysis entry), analysis.py, results/method_out.json and its full, mini and preview variants, results/notes.md, figures/ (six figures, PDF and PNG), and checks/ for independent re-derivation. Model weights and logits are kept on the run volume and are not in the published repository.

critiques.description: The calibrated ECE comparison is not like-for-like. Table 2 gives TS-SAM ECE 0.0099 and TS-SGD ECE 0.0094 at epoch 40. The per-seed TS-SAM minus TS-SGD difference recomputes to +0.0005 with mixed signs. Table 3's 'ECE, SAM minus TS-SGD' of -0.0031 compares uncalibrated SAM (0.0063) with calibrated SGD. The report still concludes that SAM has a small ECE advantage over temperature-scaled SGD. Artifact 2's scaled values point the other way (SAM 0.0070 vs SGD 0.0094 at epoch 60), and the two artifacts are not reconciled.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the TS-SAM minus TS-SGD paired row to Table 3 with CI and Holm p. Rewrite the 'What the iteration established' paragraph so the calibrated ECE result is stated as the paired TS-vs-TS comparison. Add a note that the two artifacts use different learning rates and cannot be pooled.

critiques.description: The positive claim (SAM lowers test ECE and NLL relative to SGD, and the NLL gap survives temperature scaling) has no nearest-neighbour comparison in the record. Tan et al. [4] are cited only as motivation, with no statement of what this run adds beyond them (small CNN, Fashion-MNIST, temperature-scaled control, matched-loss curvature). Morosini et al. [5] appear in the reference list but are never cited in the text, although their title ('When Calibration Follows Curvature') addresses the curvature-calibration link that Artifact 2 tests. The planned prior-work check never ran.
critiques.suggested_action: Before the positive claim is written up, add a paragraph that names Tan et al. [4] and Morosini et al. [5] as the nearest published results, states what each reports, and states what this run adds (for example, the temperature-scaled NLL control and the matched-loss Hessian comparison) and what it does not. Either cite [5] in the text or remove it from the references. Keep the prior-work direction marked as not run until it is.

critiques.description: Criterion (a) is marked as holding in the headline, but the comparison is confounded by fit: SAM ends at training loss 0.107 against 0.008 for SGD at epoch 40, and both selected learning rates sit at the lower grid edge. The report notes these as caveats, but the verdict 'Criterion (a) holds' is not scoped to them, and the only matched-loss analysis is in Artifact 2 at a different learning rate (0.03) with three seeds.
critiques.suggested_action: State the criterion (a) verdict as conditional on the fit gap in the record. If checkpoints at matched training loss exist for Artifact 1 (checkpoints/ is present in the run), run the matched-loss comparison on them and record it; otherwise say the matched comparison was not run on the headline setting.

critiques.description: Criterion (c) is marked as supported at 15 and 40 epochs using a comparison between separately trained compressed schedules (5, 15 epochs, each with its own cosine schedule) and the 40-epoch run. The CI for growth from 5 to 40 epochs (0.0435 [0.0376, 0.0494]) is computed across different schedules, not along one training trajectory, so it does not test whether the gap grows as training proceeds.
critiques.suggested_action: Report the criterion (c) result with the schedule confound stated. To test growth with training length, use checkpoints or per-epoch evaluations from the 40-epoch run at epochs 5, 15 and 40 (the per-run file already has these for the 40-epoch schedule) and report that comparison alongside the compressed one.

However, the calibrated-ECE comparison against temperature-scaled SGD is mixed across conditions (uncalibrated SAM against calibrated SGD), the like-for-like comparison is null or reversed in the same artifact, and the two artifacts disagree on calibrated ECE without reconciliation. The criterion (c) verdict and the under-fit confound are stated more firmly than the evidence supports.

The record is chronological with one iteration section and the tables are introduced by what they settle. Some labels are inconsistent (for example 'Independent independent computation' in Table 6) and the reasoning behind the iteration's design is thin.

review.overall_assessment: The record is mostly traceable and honest. I recomputed the headline paired contrasts at epoch 40 from results/per_run_metrics.csv (ECE -0.03778 [-0.04145, -0.03412]; NLL -0.09796 [-0.10918, -0.08673]; accuracy +0.00146 [-0.00071, +0.00363]; AURC -0.00152; SAM minus TS-SGD NLL -0.0209) and they match the report and results/audit_rederivation.json. The per-seed ECE differences in Table 4 also match. The Table 2 means and the Table 5 training-length advantages recompute from the per-run file. The Artifact 2 temperature-scaling means in Table 8 recompute from the per-seed values. Failed and unfinished directions are labelled. The main problems are in how the record reads its own evidence. (1) The calibrated ECE comparison is not reported like-for-like. Table 2 shows TS-SAM ECE 0.0099 against TS-SGD 0.0094 at epoch 40, which recomputes to a mean difference of +0.0005 (SAM slightly worse, per-seed signs mixed). Table 3's 'SAM minus TS-SGD' ECE of -0.0031 compares uncalibrated SAM with calibrated SGD. The report still states that SAM has a small ECE advantage over temperature-scaled SGD, and Artifact 2's scaled values (SAM 0.0070 vs SGD 0.0094) point the other way. That disagreement is not reconciled. (2) The positive claim has no nearest-neighbour comparison: the report cites Tan et al. but does not say what this run adds beyond them, and it lists Morosini et al. [5] in the references without citing it in the text, even though that paper's topic matches the curvature-calibration mechanism Artifact 2 tests. The third planned direction (prior-work check) never ran, so no novelty check exists in the record. (3) Criterion (c) is marked as holding on a comparison of separately trained compressed schedules, not a single training-length curve, and the headline comparison is confounded by under-fit SAM (train loss 0.107 vs 0.008). The caveats are written, but the verdicts are not scoped to them. (4) Some tabular output on disk is not in the report: the Artifact 1 reliability bin table (results/reliability_bins_pooled.json) and the Artifact 2 rho-ball loss increase in per_epoch.json. The reasoning that motivated the iteration is absent, as the report itself acknowledges. Results are reported from executed artifacts and I could recompute them, so results_reported is true. Soundness is 2 rather than 1: the headline claims are supported, but the calibrated-ECE claim is not reconciled with the run's own table.
strengths: Headline paired differences at epoch 40 (ECE, NLL, accuracy, AURC) recompute from results/per_run_metrics.csv to the reported values and intervals, and match results/audit_rederivation.json.

Tuning is run on a separate seed (100) with selection on validation NLL only, and the selected settings match results/chosen_hparams.json and results/tuning_table.csv; the collapsed configuration (lr 0.03, rho 0.2) is reported and excluded.
The 5-epoch reversal in the training-length test is reported as a reversal rather than hidden, and the compressed schedules are described as separate full runs.
Per-seed tables (Tables 4, 7, 11) let a reader see the sign consistency, and the report declines to give p-values for n=3.
The temperature-scaling aggregates in Table 8 recompute from the per-seed rows, and the report separates the global confidence shift from the residual NLL gap.
The unrun prior-work direction is labelled as planned but not run, with the cause given, rather than presented as a null.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this round: five-seed tuned SGD and SAM runs on a fixed Fashion-MNIST split, each with saved validation and test logits at epochs 5, 15 and final, per-model temperature-scaled SGD logits, the chosen learning rate and rho on validation, a per-epoch training-loss, ECE, NLL, and top-Hessian-eigenvalue record for three seeds per optimizer, and a sourced prior-art and baseline map. The next round evaluates paired differences, the temperature-scaling control and the overfitting dependence.
strategies.objective: Establish whether SAM lowers test calibration error and test NLL relative to a learning-rate-tuned SGD baseline on a small CNN for Fashion-MNIST, whether any such gain is a ranking improvement or only a global confidence shift, and whether the gap grows with overfitting and sharpness. The novel contribution is the temperature-scaling counterfactual applied to SAM on a small CNN, with the calibration claim tested on several metrics at once.
strategies.rationale: SAM is widely used, and its calibration benefit is argued mainly from large-model evidence (Tan et al., 2025). A small CNN on Fashion-MNIST is cheap enough to run the matched design with five seeds per optimizer and per-epoch saved predictions, so each claim can be checked on the same logits. The temperature-scaling control is the decisive step: it turns a vague calibration gain into one of two specific readings, a ranking improvement or a shrink, and both readings are publishable. Recording logits at epochs 5, 15 and final lets the next round test the training-length dependence without retraining. The strategy aims at a positive, clean result, but it is built so that a null accuracy difference and a temperature-explained calibration gap are both reportable.

artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_3
artifacts.summary: This artifact compares sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) with plain SGD for a small two-block convolutional network trained on Fashion-MNIST. Learning rates and the SAM neighbourhood size rho are chosen on a validation split only, using validation NLL, with learning rates tested below the old grid edge; the selected settings are SGD lr 0.001 and SAM lr 0.01 with rho 0.1. Five paired seeds are trained per arm, and each final model is evaluated on the official 10k test set. Reported metrics are accuracy, expected calibration error (ECE, 15 equal-width bins), negative log-likelihood (NLL), the multi-class Brier score, and a top-label equal-count adaptive calibration error (ACE). Temperature scaling fitted on validation gives a temperature-scaled SGD control and a temperature-scaled SAM row. The headline is a 12-row paired family with paired 95% t-intervals and Holm correction. SAM improves accuracy by about 1 point (a bound, not an equivalence), and its NLL is lower than temperature-scaled SGD by about 0.033 (interval excludes zero, Holm p = 0.0018). After temperature scaling, the ECE and ACE differences are not significant. Temperatures show raw SGD is over-confident and raw SAM is under-confident. Final training loss is reported beside every calibration row. The shuffled-label placebo is significant for NLL and Brier, so it does not isolate label information for confidence-sensitive metrics; this is reported as a limitation. Results apply to this dataset and this small architecture only. Outputs include method.py, the full, mini and preview method-output JSON files, tuning and analysis tables, reliability bins, logits, an independent re-derivation script, and a reproducibility guide.
artifacts.title: SAM vs SGD calibration on Fashion-MNIST

artifacts.layman_summary: We tested whether a training method called SAM makes a small image classifier more accurate and better calibrated than standard training, when the two are compared at the same level of fit.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_4
artifacts.summary: Experiment artifact testing whether sharpness-aware minimisation (SAM) improves test accuracy and calibration over plain SGD for a small CNN on Fashion-MNIST, at matched training loss. Five paired seeds (0-4). Conditions: SAM for 40 epochs with rho=0.1 (chosen on validation NLL with seed 101), SGD for 40 epochs, and SGD for E*=10 epochs (chosen so its eval-mode training loss matches SAM's 40-epoch loss within 0.01, using seed 100). Every model is temperature-scaled on validation logits. Primary comparison: SAM 40 epochs minus matched-loss SGD. Headline differences (mean of 5 paired seeds, 95% t interval, df=4): test NLL raw -0.0125 [-0.0152, -0.0099], temperature-scaled NLL -0.0082 [-0.0110, -0.0053], raw ECE (15 equal-width bins) -0.0076 [-0.0091, -0.0061], accuracy +0.0025 [+0.0007, +0.0042]. Temperature-scaled ECE shows no difference. Holm correction across the 14-test family keeps raw ECE, raw NLL, temperature-scaled NLL, Brier and ACE; accuracy is not significant after correction (p=0.055). Secondary comparison (SAM vs SGD 40-epoch snapshot at the matched epoch) shows larger differences but is weaker because mid-schedule snapshots are not finished models. Caveats: five seeds give low power; the exact sign-flip test cannot reach p<0.05 with five seeds; a label-permutation placebo passes for accuracy but not for NLL and ECE, which reward lower confidence even with uninformative labels; E*=10 sits at the lower edge of the epoch grid; the SGD learning rate was fixed at 0.01 and not re-tuned. An independent re-derivation reproduces the primary headline numbers to within 1.2e-4. Outputs: method.py and analysis.py (pipeline and statistics), audit_rederive.py, results/method_out.json, mini and preview variants, reliability diagrams and a confidence histogram in figures/, and reproducibility.md with pinned dependencies in pyproject.toml.

artifacts.layman_summary: Checks whether a sharpness-aware optimizer's calibration advantage over plain SGD grows as a small image model trains longer, using only results already saved from earlier runs.
artifacts.name: gen_art_evaluation_1
artifacts.summary: Evaluation only; no model was trained and no logits were recomputed. The script eval.py reads the declared outputs of two earlier SAM-vs-SGD runs on Fashion-MNIST and reports the paired gap (SAM minus SGD) in test and validation ECE (15 bins), NLL, accuracy, and temperature-scaled SGD controls. The two trajectories are reported separately and never pooled. Source 1 has 5 seeds at 40 epochs; its 5- and 15-epoch points come from separate compressed schedules, so its growth mixes length with schedule shape. Source 2 has 3 seeds over 60 epochs with per-epoch validation values. Results: accuracy shows no detectable difference in either source. The validation ECE and NLL gaps in source 2 are near zero at epochs 1 to 5, reach their largest mean advantage near epochs 25 to 30, and then narrow, so the epoch-60 endpoint is not the extremum. Source 1 moves from a positive ECE gap at 5 epochs to -0.038 at 40 epochs. Temperature scaling of SGD removes most of the ECE advantage; the NLL advantage persists, and at 60 epochs the NLL difference after both models are temperature-scaled is -0.016 (parametric p 0.035). Important limits: with 3 seeds the smallest exact sign-flip p-value is 0.25 and with 5 seeds 0.0625, so the parametric p-values in the table are descriptive, not evidence; the gap-versus-training-loss slopes are per-seed co-variation within one trajectory, not a test of overfitting; learning rates differ between the two sources and source 1's sit at the grid edge. An independent re-derivation of the headline numbers from raw records matched the reported values, and the placebo check rejects only at the design floor. Outputs: full, mini and preview evaluation JSON, one gap table, one six-panel figure, caveats, and reproducibility notes.

The NLL claim is kept as a lead, restated as a confidence-sensitive effect. Original wording: 'SAM's NLL gain ... reflects better ranking of confidence'. Revised: the shuffled-label placebo gap (-0.224) exceeds the true gap (-0.036), so label specificity is not shown.

critiques.description: An executed artifact is missing from the record. iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_research_1 contains research_out.json, research_report.md, research_verification.json and a reproducibility file, from a web-based prior-work search and full-text reading of Tan et al. [4], Nixon et al. [2], Guo et al. [3], Foret et al. [1] and Morosini et al. [5]. The report instead says that 'the artifact stage returned no artifact for its design' and that the prior-work check 'did not run' (Iteration 1, 'Designed but not run'). The Iteration 2 text repeats that the related-work comparison 'remains not run'. These statements contradict the volume.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the prior-work artifact to the record, with its verdict ('partly done'), the comparison table from research_report.md, and the verification outcome from research_verification.json. Remove or correct every 'did not run' and 'not run' statement, and label the actual remaining gap (for example, the claims not yet checked against the full text of the cited papers).

critiques.description: The positive NLL and ECE claims have no nearest-neighbour comparison that uses the published results. The report cites Tan et al. [4] as motivation and says that 'what this run adds' is a temperature-scaled NLL control and a matched-loss curvature comparison. The prior-work artifact (research_out.json) reports that Tan et al. already compare uncalibrated SAM ECE with calibrated SGD ECE, using temperature scaling and isotonic regression, and that SGD's ECE is about six times SAM's on ResNet-56. The 'temperature-scaled control' the report claims as new is therefore not new against that neighbour, and the report does not say so.
critiques.suggested_action: Before any positive claim is written up, add a paragraph that names Tan et al. [4] and states what it reports: the ResNet-56 ECE ratio, the temperature-scaling comparison and the tuning protocol. State what this run adds, which is restricted to the small CNN and Fashion-MNIST setting, the NLL metric, the matched-loss design and the placebo check. Also state explicitly where the run does not add to Tan et al.

critiques.description: The report misstates how the cited papers were read. It says 'neither paper was read in full in this iteration' and relies on reference summaries for Tan et al. [4] and Morosini et al. [5]. The prior-work artifact states that both were read in full from PDF text (Tan et al., arXiv 2505.23866; Morosini et al., arXiv 2604.20614). The two statements cannot both be true, and the record does not say which is correct.
critiques.suggested_action: Reconcile the two statements. Cite the prior-work artifact as the source of the full-text reading, state which sections were read, and restate the Iteration 2 reading of Tan et al. and Morosini et al. on that basis.

critiques.description: The NLL conclusion is stated more strongly than the controls allow. Artifact 3's shuffled-label control gives an NLL difference of -0.22405 (Table 14, p = 0.009). That is about six times the true-label difference of -0.03561 (Table 13). Artifact 4's placebo also fails for NLL and ECE. The report calls the control a 'limitation' and says the NLL gap 'is not, by itself, evidence that SAM uses the labels better'. It nevertheless keeps NLL as 'the most consistent result of the run' and says 'the NLL claim is kept, with a size that reflects the SGD baseline'. A placebo larger than the effect means the NLL gap is not specific to the labels.
critiques.suggested_action: Revise the 'What we have learned' section and the criterion (a) and (b) verdicts so that the NLL result is stated as a confidence-sensitive effect that the shuffled-label control does not isolate, not as the run's most consistent finding. Give the placebo-adjusted contrast or state that none was computed.

critiques.description: The matched-loss conclusion (Artifact 4) is overstated. The report says 'matching training loss means the fit gap cannot account for the NLL result in this design'. But the SGD baseline is learning rate 0.01, which the report itself records as the fourth of five SGD rates and worse on validation NLL than 0.001 (0.273 vs 0.214). The matched comparison at the validation-selected learning rate was not run. The conclusion therefore holds only for a weak baseline, and the report's own text says this.
critiques.suggested_action: Scope the matched-loss conclusion to the learning rate 0.01 baseline in the verdict. Either run the matched-loss comparison at learning rate 0.001 (the next iteration already names this), or remove the sentence that the fit gap cannot account for the NLL result.

critiques.description: Some corrections are not marked in place, and the original wording is not quoted. Correction 8 says 'a sentence about the NLL advantage is restated', and Correction 4 says 'the label is corrected', without giving the old text. Iteration 1 is then read with the corrected version in the body, so a reader cannot see what the run originally wrote.
critiques.suggested_action: For each correction, quote the original sentence or label and the new one, in place within the Iteration 1 text.

critiques.description: Table 13's Holm family of twelve contains duplicate contrasts. The 'TS-SAM minus TS-SGD' ECE and NLL rows are identical to the 'SAM minus TS-SGD' rows, as the report acknowledges. The family therefore has ten distinct tests, and the Holm adjustment is stricter than the design requires.
critiques.suggested_action: Remove the duplicate rows, or state that the family has ten distinct contrasts and recompute the Holm p values over that family.

critiques.description: Some outputs on disk are not reported and some reported numbers are not recomputed. Artifact 4's tuning.json gives the full grid for seed 101, but the report gives only three radius values. Artifact 3's selection.json and posthoc_placebo_ts.json are not cited. Artifact 2's results/notes.md and checks/ are not cited. Table 10 (matched-loss per seed) and Table 15 (per-condition means) were not recomputed from their records in this review.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the Artifact 4 tuning grid (or reference tuning.json by path) and cite the Artifact 2 and Artifact 3 check and selection files. Mark Table 10 and Table 15 as artifact-summary values if they are not recomputed.

dimension_scores.justification: Recomputed headline numbers match, but the NLL verdict ('most consistent result', 'NLL claim is kept') is stated more strongly than the Artifact 3 and Artifact 4 placebo checks allow, and the matched-loss test is run only on the weakest SGD baseline. The record also misstates what the prior-work step did.

Tables are introduced by what they settle and the iterations are in order. Corrections are marked, but some are listed at the end and not in place, and a few sentences are restated without the original wording.

The report omits a completed artifact (iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_research_1) whose prior-work search and verification are the nearest-neighbour check the record needs. It also drops from the record the fact that the check ran, and lists it as not run. Experiments 1 to 4 and Evaluation 1 are otherwise well recorded.

review.overall_assessment: The record's executed numbers hold up. I recomputed Artifact 1's epoch-40 paired contrasts (accuracy, ECE, NLL), the compressed-schedule contrasts and the epoch-5/15 within-run gaps from per_run_metrics.csv, and they match the report to the reported digits. I also recomputed Artifact 3's Table 13 ECE row from analysis_tables.json and Artifact 4's matched-loss gaps (Table 16) from matched_loss_table.json; both match. The Hessian ratios in Table 22 are arithmetically correct from the table's own values. Results are reported from artifacts that ran, and most corrections are marked in place. The record has four problems that matter. (1) It omits an executed artifact: iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_research_1 (research_out.json, research_report.md, research_verification.json) is a completed prior-work search and verification, yet the report says the prior-work check 'did not run' and 'the artifact stage returned no artifact'. (2) It says neither Tan et al. nor Morosini et al. was read in full, while that artifact says both were read in full from PDF text; the nearest-neighbour comparison that the record lacks is in that artifact. That artifact also reports that Tan et al. already compare uncalibrated SAM ECE with temperature-scaled SGD, which undercuts the 'temperature-scaled control' the report offers as what this run adds. (3) The NLL claim is kept as 'the most consistent result', but Artifact 3's shuffled-label NLL gap (-0.224) is about six times the true-label gap (-0.036), and Artifact 4's placebo also fails for NLL. The report calls this a limitation but does not let it change the verdict. (4) The matched-loss conclusion ('the fit gap cannot account for the NLL result') rests on an SGD baseline the report itself calls the weakest of five. Coverage of the user's question (train the models and compare accuracy and calibration) is full. Soundness is 2 rather than 1: the headline numbers are real and reproducible, but the NLL conclusion is stated more strongly than the placebo allows. Not blocking, since results are reported and recomputed.
strengths: Headline paired contrasts in Artifact 1 (accuracy, ECE, NLL at epoch 40, and the compressed 5- and 15-epoch rows) recompute exactly from per_run_metrics.csv, so the core numbers are traceable.
Artifact 3's Table 13 ECE row (-0.00500, CI, p = 0.0084) and Artifact 4's per-seed matched-loss gaps (Table 16) recompute from the artifacts' own records.

The record reverses its own earlier claims in place: the uncalibrated-versus-calibrated ECE comparison, the accuracy null tied to a single SGD learning rate, and the 5-epoch reversal caused by separate schedules. Each reversal is written down with the evidence that caused it.
Evaluation 1 explicitly corrects its own artifact's summary (the epoch 1 to 2 NLL gap), and the report follows the gap table rather than the summary.
Table 22's Hessian ratios are correct from the table's own values, and the report corrects its earlier 'two to three times at every epoch' wording.
The report keeps the limitations of five and three seeds and the absence of exact p-values below 0.0625, and does not treat parametric p-values as evidence.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this round: a retuned table over learning rates below the old grid edge; five-seed headline results at the retuned settings with raw, temperature-scaled and TS-SAM minus TS-SGD paired contrasts; a matched-loss comparison with per-epoch logits and a shortened-schedule SGD control, five seeds; and a single-schedule trajectory table for the training-length question. Together these decide whether the NLL lead holds on the threats named in the record, and whether the calibration gap grows with training.
strategies.objective: Establish whether SAM's test NLL advantage over SGD on a small CNN for Fashion-MNIST survives the two open threats to it, learning rates tuned beyond the grid edge and matched training loss, and whether the SAM-SGD calibration gap grows along one training trajectory. The contribution is a calibration and NLL comparison in which every model is temperature-scaled on validation and the fit confound is controlled directly.
strategies.rationale: The NLL lead survived temperature scaling of SGD, which is the one result that can carry a ranking-level claim. Its two open threats are that SAM is under-fit at epoch 40 (training loss 0.107 against 0.008) and that both selected learning rates (0.01) sit at the lower grid edge. Testing both on the headline setting is the cheapest decisive step. The shift from the previous round is that the question is now answered at matched fit and with tuning that is not truncated by the grid, not at matched epochs alone. The training-length question is answered by a cheap evaluation of trajectories already on record, not by new models. The prior-work check (Tan et al., 2025; Morosini et al., 2026) is not funded this round and stays marked as not run in the report.
